newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Hoogovens profit down, tops forecast.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Hoogovens profit down, tops forecast.

text.p: Steel and aluminium group Hoogovens NV announced a sharp fall in 1996 net profit on Thursday but its earnings were above market expectations and the firm said it was upbeat about the outlook for 1997.
Net profit fell to 326 million guilders ($169 million) from 507 million in 1995 but analysts had forecast only 260 to 310 million. The company said it would pay an unchanged divided of 3.00 guilders.
Immediately after the results, Hoogovens shares jumped seven guilders to 98.00 but profit-taking later drove the price back to 93.00 for a gain of two guilders.
Earnings were hit by lower selling prices for both steel and aluminium, while margins at metal-processing units were squeezed due to slack demand for rolled and extruded products.
Hoogovens chairman Maarten van Veen said results for the second half of the year had exceeded the company's own expectations due to a mild upturn in demand and lower taxes.
Van Veen was moderately optimistic about the outlook for the current year, predicting that net profit from ordinary activities would improve compared with 1996.

"On the basis of current forecasts, the recovery of the economy in Europe will result in moderate economic growth in 1997, with a positive impact on demand for steel and aluminium products," he told a news conference.
"Although the increase in demand has not yet resulted in a satisfactory improvement in prices, price levels may be expected to increase in the course of the year," he said.
Pre-tax profits from steel fell to 427 million guilders from 720 million in 1995, while pre-tax profits from aluminium dropped to 43 million guilders from 140 million.
Van Veen said the aluminium division's return on capital invested remained too low at six percent.

He said Hoogovens had no plans to withdraw from aluminium but it was willing to let one or more of its aluminium units form joint ventures with other companies if that would lead to mutual benefits for the companies involved.
Steel chief Ad van der Velden said Hoogovens planned to invest 500 million guilders in the coming years in a new "thin slab caster" which will be in full production by the year 2000.
The thin slab caster will reduce costs by integrating the processes of continuous casting and hot-rolling which are separate under the conventional production method.
It will have an annual capacity of 1.5 million tonnes, of which about one million will represent an expansion of capacity.
Hoogovens has recently taken a 50 percent stake in Belgian steel firm UGB and raised its stake in German steel-processing firm Hille & Mueller to 100 percent from 50 percent.
Van Veen said further acqusitions were possible in 1997, though they were likely to be far smaller than these deals.
Analysts were generally positive about the results and the accompanying statement about prospects for 1997.
"The future for Hoogovens looks good, the economy is improving, steel prices are good and financially the company is very sound," said Peter Wortel of Delta Lloyd Bank.
